terms.comment: The “sounding” letter, littera understood, so feminine. A vowel is long by nature or by position, vōcālis est longa nātūrā aut positiōne (Traupman 247; positiōne longa, Quint. 1.5.28).

phrases.latin: nōn quia magnae sit operae cōnsonantēs ā vōcālibus discernere
phrases.english: not because it is a great labour to tell consonants from vowels

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 247, 248, 249.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
